newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures steady in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures steady in featureless trade.

text.p: IPE Brent futures traded quietly and with little direction on Monday in the wake of the hectic expiry last week of the July contract, brokers said.
By 1430 GMT August futures were up eight cents at $17.82 a barrel, with gas oil trailing along, down $1.75 a tonne at $161.
In New York the front-month West Texas Intermediate contract stood 12 cents up at $18.95 in early trade.
"We had a pretty active expiry on Friday and it looks as though that has taken the sting out of the market for a day or two," said one broker. "In the short-term I think we are range bound."
Brokers said business was likely to waver between resistance at around $17.85-$17.90 and support down at the $17.40 level.
"It doesn't look as though it wants to go anywhere at the moment," said one futures dealer.

Active players discounted the uncertainty over the technicalities of renewing Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, although some said it was providing a fundamental base from which the market could move higher.
Baghdad's U.N. envoy Nizar Hamdoon said on Friday Iraq had no interest in delaying its oil sales, but wanted assurances on U.N plans to distribute food and medicine bought with the proceeds.
It is still unclear when Iraqi exports will restart and Baghdad has become uncooperative in its dealings with the world body over the last week.
Gas oil was said to be off on fund selling amplified by the thinness of trade. Some of the fall was a catch up with a late dip in Brent prices on Friday after the gas oil close.
